story.title: The Seat at the Counter
story.scene: a port tavern at night. the counter runs along one wall. behind it, shelves of bottles catch the lamplight. three stools face the counter. the door opens onto the dark harbor.

steps.text: You kept my seat. Even after what I did?
Three years I've been gone. You saved it?
Night we met, you spilled wine on that guy's vest.
And you threw him out. Told him to find another tavern.
Been saving your seat ever since. Where else would you sit?
One day I'm opening my own place. Not pouring for someone else.
I know how to make that happen.
You've said that before.
This time I mean it. You own a ship someday. Command it yourself.
Where did James go that night?
He ran. Because he stole the cargo.
I don't know that. I was drunk.
Tomorrow, harbor court. Sunrise. I need you to testify.
Testify to what?
That you saw James loading stolen goods that night before he vanished.
If you testify, you're saying James was a thief.
What do you want me to do?
I'm against this. I won't watch it.
If you testify, the partnership starts. The ship is yours to chase.
And if I don't?
I walk away from you. No ship. No partnership. Nothing.

then.text: See you at sunrise. We walk to court together.

choice.t: Ask for time. Need to remember.
choice.say: I need time. That night was fuzzy. I don't remember clearly.

then.text: I want to get this right.

steps.text: Saturday, after the hearing. We'll talk about everything. The ship. The plan.
After we're done at court.
Or never. Depends what you do up there.

next: If he promised to testify: Le_pirate walks to the courthouse at sunrise; Lily pulls Justin aside in the dark and says she loves him for staying honest—but he just lied to her face.

If he asked for time: Le_pirate arrives before dawn, overhears Justin telling Lily he can't testify because he was too drunk to remember anything; Le_pirate leaves the tavern without a word, and by the time Justin follows him outside, the ship is already untying its lines.
